title: Neural Evidence and Behavioural Welfare Economics: When Can Neuroeconomics Inform Policy?
abstract: arXiv:2511.19548v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Neuroeconomics appears to offer welfare economics an evidential supplement, since neural data may help distinguish choices that express genuine preferences from choices distorted by addiction, framing or self-control failure. This paper asks when such evidence can legitimately inform welfare judgements for policy. It develops a conceptual framework linking three levels of analysis, namely neural signals, computational decision models and normative welfare criteria. The central argument is that neural data can constrain welfare analysis only under four conditions, covering the validity of the neural measure, the identifiability of the decision model, the explicit statement of the welfare criterion, and the institutional context of any policy use. translated_title: 神经证据与行为福利经济学：神经经济学何时能为政策提供依据？
translated_abstract: 神经经济学似乎为福利经济学提供了一种证据上的补充，因为神经数据可能有助于区分表达真实偏好的选择与因成瘾、框架效应或自控失败而扭曲的选择。本文探讨这种证据何时才能合法地为政策的福利判断提供依据。本文构建了一个将三个分析层面联系起来的概念框架，即神经信号、计算决策模型和规范性福利标准。核心论点是：神经数据只有在满足四个条件时才能约束福利分析，这四个条件涵盖神经测量的有效性、决策模型的可识别性、福利标准的明确陈述，以及任何政策应用的制度背景。本文将该框架应用于成瘾、神经营销和环境政策领域，并以英国《2026年烟草与电子烟法案》为例展开分析，这是一项在缺乏相应依据的情况下进行正当化论证的重大干预措施。
tldr: 本文提出一个连接神经信号、计算决策模型与规范性福利标准的概念框架，论证神经数据只有在神经测量有效、决策模型可识别、福利标准明确陈述且考虑政策制度背景这四个条件下才能合法地为政策福利判断提供依据。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a conceptual framework linking neural signals, computational decision models, and normative welfare criteria, arguing that neural data can legitimately inform policy welfare judgements only under four conditions: validity of the neural measure, identifiability of the decision model, explicit statement of the welfare criterion, and the institutional context of policy use.
